text:
COP rose 0.88% today to $139.07, continuing a rebound from last week's lows as oil prices stabilized. The U.S. oil benchmark is trading at $99.64 per barrel, still well below the $107+ level seen earlier, but the worst of last week's sell-off appears to have passed. Trump's comments over the weekend that the Iran conflict would end "fairly soon" sparked initial optimism about de-escalation, which had briefly pushed crude down; today's modest gain suggests the market has digested that news and is finding a floor.

The two-week decline of 7.3% reflects the broader whipsaw in energy stocks as geopolitical risk around Iran has shifted rapidly from crisis to potential resolution. While Trump administration officials have sent mixed signals—with Secretary of State Rubio still skeptical of diplomatic progress—the simple fact that resolution talk has replaced strike fears has taken pressure off oil prices and energy stocks that benefit from higher crude.
